title: kdash korg pulse
description: Payload of kdash:korg:pulse — latest-value TS-OWNED (STRING JSON, no TTL), exactly 3 segments, on central (KDASH_CENTRAL_REDIS). The korg backlog at a glance: how many work items are open, how that number moved over 30 days, the three lane counts, and how the open items split across projects. Contract v1 (CD-28), the first built key of CD-26's kdash:korg:* family. The consumers are kpidash's korg + klams card (which reads open, history, awaiting, active and by_project) and a standalone korg card (which adds queued and the projects count); the fuller set is contracted now so the standalone card needs no version bump. Written by a publisher that reads korg's own rollups and COPIES korg's figures, never re-deriving them (CD-26). Freshness is reader-owned: the writer publishes its own cadence in `expected_refresh_s` and the reader greys the card once `ts` is older than that plus its grace (kdash_cadence_stale). Field names are pinned; a rename, retype or removal lands as kdash:korg:v2:pulse (rules.md Versioning), never in place.

ts.description: Unix seconds (float) when the publisher read korg, writer's clock. Bounded at 1e11 so a millisecond stamp fails instead of reading as permanently fresh.

expected_refresh_s.description: How long the publisher expects between its own writes, in seconds. The reader greys the record once `ts` is older than this plus its own grace — the claude:limits rule, made the default for this family (CD-28).

open.description: korg's backlog: work items in any non-terminal status (open, resolved, done, parked), unarchived, all projects. Exactly the figure korg's work_item_flow reports as today's `backlog` and list_work_items reports as `total` — copied, never recounted. Equal to the last `history` entry's `open` whenever `history` is non-empty.

projects.description: How many projects hold at least one of the `open` items. Always >= the length of `by_project`; the difference is how many projects the cap left out.

awaiting.description: Length of korg's Awaiting Ken lane (list_awaiting / the board's `awaiting`). korg's own name for it; kfdc calls the same lane Commander's Call.

active.description: Sprint proposals in status `active` (the board's `active` list).

queued.description: Sprint proposals in status `proposed` — the Planning queue, kfdc's On Deck. Parked proposals are not counted: they are not startable.

by_project.description: Open items per project, LARGEST FIRST (ties by name, ascending), at most 24 entries; projects with no open item are omitted. The card shows the first entry as the top project and draws one bar segment per entry. Overflow is never silent: items in projects past the cap, and items with no project at all, are counted in `other_open`. Empty only when `open` is 0 or every open item is unassigned.

open.description: That project's share of `open`, by the same definition.

other_open.description: Open items NOT in any `by_project` entry: those in projects past the 24-entry cap, plus those with no project. 0 when everything is listed. The sum of every `by_project[].open` plus `other_open` is `open` — a producer obligation the validator cannot check (no arithmetic keywords, CD-24).

history.description: Daily backlog, OLDEST FIRST, at most 30 entries, the last being today in korg's board timezone. Copied from korg's work_item_flow `backlog` column. May be shorter than 30, or empty, while korg's transition log does not reach back that far: missing days are absent, never zero-filled, because a 0 is a real backlog level.

date.description: Calendar date in korg's board timezone, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

open.description: The backlog at that day's end (today: at `ts`).

x-counterexamples.why: `other_open` absent: the overflow count is required even when it is 0, because a feed that caps a list must say what the cap left out (CD-26), and absence is indistinguishable from a publisher that forgot
25 `by_project` entries: the cap is 24 and the 25th project belongs in `other_open`, not on the wire as a segment the card has no room for
`ts` in milliseconds reads as a record from the far future, which readers treat as clock skew and therefore fresh — a dead publisher would never go stale
history dates are ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`; a locale-formatted date sorts wrongly and the card cannot label the axis from it
a project with no open item is omitted, not listed at 0 — a zero-width segment is still a segment, and the gap it leaves is a bar that lies
`expected_refresh_s` absent: this family's staleness is the writer's own cadence plus the reader's grace, so a record that does not say its cadence cannot be judged stale at all
